dimensions.assessment: Affects the operations of the Government Accountability Office, the Congressional Budget Office, and congressional committees reporting legislation.
dimensions.evidence: To require the Comptroller General of the United States to analyze certain legislation in order to prevent duplication of and overlap with existing Federal programs, offices, and initiatives.

dimensions.assessment: Creates procedural requirements for analyzing and reporting potential legislative duplication as a supplement to CBO cost estimates.
dimensions.evidence: the Director may include the information submitted by the Comptroller General... as a supplement to the estimate for the covered bill or joint resolution

dimensions.assessment: Does not appropriate funds or authorize new spending, relying instead on existing agency analytical capabilities.
Amends title 31 of the United States Code to mandate a new analytical process for all public bills and joint resolutions reported by congressional committees.
dimensions.evidence: Section 719 of title 31, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a permanent procedural requirement for future congressional legislation upon taking effect.
dimensions.evidence: The amendment made by this Act shall take effect on the earlier of... the date on which a new Congress begins after the date that is 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act.

importance_detail.rationale: The bill establishes an administrative assessment and reporting requirement for the Government Accountability Office and the Congressional Budget Office regarding legislative duplication, altering internal congressional workflow without directly changing substantive public programs.
